tagline: Your Bridge Between Hawaiʻi and Home

lead.headline: Honolulu Harbor reopens as Hawaiʻi transportation recovery advances
lead.summary: HDOT says Honolulu Harbor reopened at 9:30 a.m. Wednesday after the Coast Guard cleared the harbor entrance, while recovery work continues on Kauaʻi and Lānaʻi.
lead.why_it_matters: Reopening Honolulu Harbor restores a key statewide cargo gateway after Lowell, while residents and businesses should note that some neighbor-island transportation infrastructure remains under repair.
body: Honolulu Harbor reopened Wednesday morning as Hawaiʻi transportation agencies continued restoring infrastructure affected by Hurricane Lowell. The Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation said the U.S. Coast Guard Captain of the Port reopened the harbor at 9:30 a.m. after the entrance had been closed because of broken buoys.

The reopening is significant because Honolulu Harbor is a major gateway for goods moving through the state. HDOT’s September 9 update shows that recovery is progressing, but conditions are not uniform across the islands. Port Allen on Kauaʻi remained closed at the time of the agency update.

On Kauaʻi, crews restored an emergency access lane on Kūhiō Highway at Hanalei Bridge. HDOT also reported ongoing work around the Wailua River Bridge, where debris removal and traffic controls have affected normal travel patterns. Residents and visitors should continue to follow current HDOT notices before traveling through recovery areas.

On Lānaʻi, repairs at Kaumālapaʻu Harbor include work on a sinkhole, the pier apron and debris in the waterway. HDOT revised its estimate for those repairs to about two weeks and said it is working with community partners on alternatives for delivery of consumer goods while vessel operations are disrupted.

For Oʻahu readers, the immediate takeaway is that Honolulu Harbor is open again. For families, businesses and travelers connected to Kauaʻi or Lānaʻi, however, storm recovery continues and some transportation limitations remain. Conditions can change as inspections and repairs progress, so official HDOT and Coast Guard updates remain the best source for operational status.

stories.headline: Hawaiian Electric shifts crews to Kauaʻi as Oʻahu restoration nears completion
stories.summary: Hawaiian Electric says nearly all Oʻahu customers affected by Lowell have been restored and teams are preparing to assist Kauaʻi recovery efforts.
stories.why_it_matters: The utility response is moving from broad Oʻahu restoration toward targeted recovery support for Kauaʻi, where storm impacts remain more substantial.
body: Hawaiian Electric is shifting part of its post-storm response toward Kauaʻi after reporting that power restoration for customers affected by Hurricane Lowell on Oʻahu is nearly complete. The company said Wednesday that it is preparing personnel, vehicles and equipment to support Kauaʻi Island Utility Cooperative, the separate utility serving Kauaʻi.

The first Hawaiian Electric team is expected to arrive on Kauaʻi Thursday to assist with damage assessments and help determine what supplies and equipment are needed. Trucks and other equipment are expected to arrive by barge Friday, according to the utility’s September 9 release.

The move follows substantial restoration progress on Oʻahu. Earlier Wednesday, Hawaiian Electric reported that another 1,060 customers had been restored overnight and about 440 remained without service at 6:30 a.m. The company’s later update said nearly all Oʻahu customers affected by Lowell had been restored.

Some individual customers can still face property-level electrical damage even after the surrounding grid is repaired. Hawaiian Electric has advised customers without service to check their main circuit breaker and, where necessary, have privately owned electrical equipment repaired before reconnection can safely occur.

For PinoyLink Hawaiʻi readers, the broader recovery picture is improving on Oʻahu while assistance is being redirected to Kauaʻi. Families with connections to Kauaʻi should continue following Kauaʻi Island Utility Cooperative and county emergency information for local restoration timelines, because conditions there are separate from Hawaiian Electric’s Oʻahu system.
